# Interactive

<span data-language-key="interactive"></span>

No install and no account. Each of these runs in your browser, in English or
Spanish, and answers a question the pages can only describe: move a control and
the shapes, the strides and the numbers move with it. Every one is also linked
from the section it belongs to, in the [handbook](./tensors_workshop_plan_with_quizzes.html)
and on the [notebooks page](notebooks.qmd).

:::: {.widget-grid}
::: {.resource-card}
### 🧮 Broadcasting simulator

<span data-language-key="broadcasting-simulator"></span>

Type two shapes. Watch NumPy line them up from the right, pad the short one, and
stretch every axis of size 1 — or refuse, and say which axis. Section 03.

[Try shapes](interactive/broadcasting-simulator.html?lang=en){.resource-button}
:::

::: {.resource-card}
### 🧊 The image tensor

<span data-language-key="image-tensor"></span>

Three real photos as one 4-D tensor, a cube per byte. Transpose it and watch
the shape and strides permute while the picture stays; reshape it and watch
the picture break; rewrite the buffer C, Fortran or channels_last and watch
only the memory move. Every click prints the NumPy and PyTorch that does it.
Section 04.

Straight to [transpose](interactive/image-tensor.html?lang=en#transpose),
[reshape](interactive/image-tensor.html?lang=en#reshape) or
[the memory layout](interactive/image-tensor.html?lang=en#memory).

[Open the image tensor](interactive/image-tensor.html?lang=en){.resource-button}
:::

::: {.resource-card}
### 👁️ Attention as two contractions

<span data-language-key="attention-stage"></span>

Seven pictures of one sequence, every number small enough to add up by hand:
four ids gathered out of an embedding table, that table projected three ways
into Q, K and V, each split so every head gets its own axis — a reshape that
has to be a transpose too, and the bug when it is not — the contraction that
makes the scores, softmax turning them into weights that sum to one, the
weighted average that is the output, and the rank-4 tensor a real model is
handed. Sections 04 and 06, and Appendix B.

Straight to [every head gets its own axis](interactive/attention-stage.html?lang=en#heads),
[the scores](interactive/attention-stage.html?lang=en#scores) or
[softmax](interactive/attention-stage.html?lang=en#softmax).

[Open the attention stage](interactive/attention-stage.html?lang=en){.resource-button}
:::

::: {.resource-card}
### 📐 Projection & SVD stage

<span data-language-key="projection-svd-stage"></span>

Least squares is a projection: scroll, and watch a target vector's shadow land
on the plane its predictors span, with the residual meeting it at a right
angle. Then the SVD portal, where a unit circle becomes an ellipse and
A v = σ u stops being notation, and on to the eigenvectors, two nearly
collinear columns and float32 dividing by exactly zero. One problem, sections
07, 08 and 09.

Straight to [the SVD portal](interactive/linalg-stage.html?lang=en#portal),
[the eigenvectors](interactive/linalg-stage.html?lang=en#eigen) or
[float32 dividing by zero](interactive/linalg-stage.html?lang=en#precision).

[Open the projection & SVD stage](interactive/linalg-stage.html?lang=en){.resource-button}
:::

::: {.resource-card}
### 🎙️ The audio tensor

<span data-language-key="voice-tensor-stage"></span>

Air becomes numbers: 48 000 a second, each rounded to 16 bits, written down as
an array you can listen to. Then one window is cut out of it, the transform is
asked which frequencies are in that window, and the window hops along to build
a frequency-by-time matrix, 513 × 465 — and you can hear what a transpose does
to it. It ends on the rank-4 batch a model is handed, three recordings stacked.
Sections 00, 02, 04 and 09, and Appendix E.

Straight to [one window](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#frame),
[the transform](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#spectrum),
[the best rank-k there is](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#lowrank) or
[the batch](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en#batch).

[Open the audio tensor](interactive/voice-stage.html?lang=en){.resource-button}
:::
::: {.resource-card}
### 🚕 Tucker and CP

<span data-language-key="tucker-cp-stage"></span>

One real tensor, factorised two ways: 6,383 New York taxi trips, pickup borough
by dropoff borough by hour of day. Unfold that cube three ways, take the SVD of
each unfolding, and reassemble a small core plus three factor matrices — 480
numbers down to 102, at 6.7% error, the hour factor peaking at 18 though nothing
ever told it what an hour is. Then build a rank-1 term out of three vectors,
find several at once with alternating least squares, and spend one parameter
budget both ways. Sections 10 and 11, and Appendix C.

Straight to [the core and its three factors](interactive/factor-stage.html?lang=en#tucker),
[one rank-1 term](interactive/factor-stage.html?lang=en#rank1) or
[the same budget spent two ways](interactive/factor-stage.html?lang=en#budget).

[Open Tucker and CP](interactive/factor-stage.html?lang=en){.resource-button}
:::
